question: In ice hockey, the fences that surround the ice hockey rink are called as _______.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Boards**__.
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
 __ 
• **Boards** refer to the protective barriers surrounding an ice hockey rink. These barriers are crucial for player safety and maintaining the flow of the game. 
• The **boards** are typically made of wood or high-density polyethylene (HDPE) and are designed to be sturdy enough to withstand impacts from players and pucks. 
• They are an integral part of the rink, ensuring the puck remains within the playing area and does not disrupt the game by leaving the surface. 
• Boards also have **plexiglass panels** mounted above them to allow spectators to view the game while providing additional safety against stray pucks. 
• This feature enables the game to progress without interruptions, as the puck rebounds off the boards and stays within the playing area. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
 __ 
• **Zones:** 
• In ice hockey, the rink is divided into three zones: **defensive zone, neutral zone, and offensive zone**. 
• These zones help in determining strategies and offsides during the game. 
• However, zones do not refer to the physical structures like boards around the rink. 
• **Crease:** 
• The "crease" is the semi-circular area in front of the goal where the goalie is allowed to operate freely. 
• It is marked on the ice and does not involve any physical barriers like the boards. 
• **Spikes:** 
• Spikes are not a term associated with ice hockey rinks or their surrounding structures. 
• They may refer to the sharp points on ice skates but have no relevance to the rink's barriers. 
• **Features of Ice Hockey Rinks:** 
• Standard rinks are **200 feet long** and **85 feet wide** as per NHL regulations. 
• The boards are usually **4 feet high**, with transparent plexiglass extending another 5-8 feet above them. 
• The rink also includes markings for face-off circles, blue lines dividing zones, and goal lines. 
• **Role of Boards in Gameplay:** 
• Boards ensure the puck remains in play, enabling the fast-paced nature of ice hockey. 
• They are also used tactically by players to pass the puck or check opponents. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**
 
• The **boards** and plexiglass ensure the safety of spectators and players during the game. 
• They are built to absorb impacts, reducing the risk of injuries to players. 
• In international ice hockey, the rink dimensions may differ slightly, but the boards remain a constant feature. 
• Boards often feature advertisements, making them a source of revenue for teams and leagues. </ul
